claim: The HSA promoter induced robust over-expression of Errγ in the Mtn-/- background.
source: Firstly, we found that the HSA promoter used induced robust over-expression of Errγ in the Mtn-/- background (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A demonstrating ERRγ mRNA levels.

claim: The body mass of WT, Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ animals was similar at 12 weeks of age.
source: The body mass of WT, Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ animals was similar at 12 weeks of age (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of body mass shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The EDL muscle was approximately 43% larger in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT.
source: However, the EDL, gastrocnemius, soleus and TA muscles were in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ approximately 43%, 44%, 47% and 70% larger than their WT counterpart, respectively (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of muscle mass shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The gastrocnemius muscle was approximately 44% larger in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT.
source: However, the EDL, gastrocnemius, soleus and TA muscles were in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ approximately 43%, 44%, 47% and 70% larger than their WT counterpart, respectively (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of muscle mass shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The soleus muscle was approximately 47% larger in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT.
source: However, the EDL, gastrocnemius, soleus and TA muscles were in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ approximately 43%, 44%, 47% and 70% larger than their WT counterpart, respectively (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of muscle mass shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The TA muscle was approximately 70% larger in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT.
source: However, the EDL, gastrocnemius, soleus and TA muscles were in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ approximately 43%, 44%, 47% and 70% larger than their WT counterpart, respectively (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of muscle mass shown in Figure 1F.

claim: There was no significant difference in mass for any of the muscles from Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice.
source: Importantly, there was no significant difference in mass for any of the muscles from Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of muscle mass measurements shown in Figure 1C-F.

claim: Mtn-/- mice performed worse than WT in the running to exhaustion protocol on a treadmill.
source: Using the running to exhaustion protocol on a treadmill, we found that Mtn-/- mice performed worse than WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from exercise tolerance testing.

claim: Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice ran for approximately 80% longer than the Mtn-/- mice.
source: However the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ ran for approximately 80% longer than the Mtn-/- and 25% longer than the WT mice (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from exercise tolerance testing shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice ran for approximately 25% longer than the WT mice.
source: However the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ ran for approximately 80% longer than the Mtn-/- and 25% longer than the WT mice (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from exercise tolerance testing shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The maximal isometric tetanic force generated by the EDL of Mtn-/- was not significantly different from that of the WT mice, despite the larger muscle mass.
source: We found that the maximal isometric tetanic force generated by the EDL of Mtn-/- was not significantly different from that of the WT mice, despite the larger muscle mass (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of tetanic force shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The tetanic force generated by Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ EDL was greater than that of the EDL from both WT and Mtn-/- mice.
source: The tetanic force generated by Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ EDL was, however, greater than that of the EDL from both WT and Mtn-/- mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of tetanic force.

claim: The specific force of the EDL of Mtn-/- mice was lower than that of the other groups.
source: The sPo of the EDL of Mtn-/- mice was lower that of the other groups, with that of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice being significantly greater than Mtn-/- mice, but not normalized to WT levels (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of specific force shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The specific force of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice was significantly greater than Mtn-/- mice, but not normalized to WT levels.
source: The sPo of the EDL of Mtn-/- mice was lower that of the other groups, with that of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice being significantly greater than Mtn-/- mice, but not normalized to WT levels (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of specific force shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The tetanic force of Mtn-/- soleus muscle was significantly lower than those of WT.
source: The tetanic force of Mtn-/- soleus muscle was significantly lower than those of WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of soleus tetanic force.

claim: There was no difference in tetanic force between the soleus muscles of WT and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+.
source: There was no difference in this parameter between the soleus muscles of WT and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The increased muscle mass in Mtn-/- mice are due to both hypertrophy and hyperplasia.
source: The increased muscle mass in Mtn-/- mice are due to both hypertrophy and hyperplasia.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about myostatin null mice and is supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- did not significantly change the number of fibres normally seen in Mtn-/- EDL.
source: We found that the introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- did not significantly change the number of fibres normally seen in Mtn-/- EDL (Figure 2A–B) or soleus muscles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B) both of which were greater than in WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of fibre number shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: The introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- did not significantly change the number of fibres normally seen in Mtn-/- soleus muscles.
source: We found that the introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- did not significantly change the number of fibres normally seen in Mtn-/- EDL (Figure 2A–B) or soleus muscles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B) both of which were greater than in WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of fibre number shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: The fibre sizes were equivalent in the EDL of Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice.
source: The fibre sizes were equivalent in the EDL of Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of fibre cross-sectional area.

claim: The MHCIIB fibres in the EDL were approximately 270% larger in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT.
source: Of particular note was that the MHCIIB fibres in the EDL were approximately 270% larger in both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of fibre cross-sectional area shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The MHCIIA fibres in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ were smaller than in Mtn-/-, but they were still larger than those in the WT.
source: The other notable result was the smaller size of MHCIIA fibres in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than Mtn-/-, but they were still larger than those in the WT (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of fibre cross-sectional area shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- caused a partial reversal of MHC profile of Mtn-/- towards the WT condition in all muscles examined.
source: Introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- caused a partial reversal of MHC profile of Mtn-/- towards the WT condition in all muscles examined (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of MHC fibre type composition shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and C.

claim: The MHC conversion was only detected within the MHCII subtypes but did not extend to normalization of the proportion of MHCI fibres.
source: This conversion was only detected within the MHCII subtypes but did not extend to normalization of the proportion of MHCI fibres; in the soleus of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+, the proportion of MHCIIB fibres was lower than that in Mtn-/- while that of MHCIIA fibres was higher.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of MHC fibre type composition.

claim: Both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ display a lower proportion of MHCI fibres in the soleus muscle than WT.
source: Nevertheless, both Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ display a lower proportion of MHCI fibres in the soleus muscle than WT (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of MHC fibre type composition shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The levels of phosphorylated Akt were higher in the muscle of Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT.
source: We found that the levels of phosphorylated Akt (an inducer of anabolism) were higher in the muscle of Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A similar relationship was discovered for 4EBP1, a downstream target of Akt.
source: A similar relationship was discovered for its downstream target 4EBP1 (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Deletion of Mtn resulted in an increased ratio of the inactive:active (phosphorylated:non-phosphorylated) form of FoxO3.
source: We found that deletion of Mtn resulted in an increased ratio of the inactive:active (phosphorylated:non-phosphorylated) form of FoxO3.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis of FoxO3 phosphorylation.

claim: In muscles of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice the levels of inactive FoxO3 were lower than in that of the Mtn-/-.
source: However, in muscles of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice the levels of inactive FoxO3 were lower than in that of the Mtn-/- (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In all muscles examined, the intensity of the SDH staining of fibres was lower in muscle from Mtn-/- compared to WT.
source: In all muscles examined, the intensity of the SDH staining (measure of oxidative activity) of fibres was lower in muscle from Mtn-/- compared to WT (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by SDH histochemistry shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Upon over-expression of Errγ, the intensity of SDH staining in fibres of Mtn-/- muscle was restored to that of WT.
source: However, upon over-expression of Errγ, the intensity of SDH staining in fibres of Mtn-/- muscle was restored to that of WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by SDH histochemistry analysis.

claim: The number of SDH positive fibres was higher in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than that seen in even the WT muscles albeit not significantly so.
source: Indeed, also the number of SDH positive fibres was higher than that seen in even the WT muscles albeit not significantly so (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by SDH histochemistry analysis shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- caused normalization of the number PAS positive fibres.
source: Introduction of Errγ into Mtn-/- also caused normalization of the number PAS positive fibres (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by PAS staining analysis shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The capillary to fibre ratio was lowest in the muscles of Mtn-/- mice and highest in those of the Mtn-/-ErrγTg/+ mice.
source: The capillary to fibre ratio (C:F); was lowest in the muscles of Mtn-/- mice and highest in those of the Mtn-/-ErrγTg/+ mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by capillary density measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A clear clustering was observed in the PCA scores plot comparing all three genotypic groups demonstrating that they had distinctive metabolite profiles.
source: A clear clustering was observed in the scores plot comparing all three genotypic groups demonstrating that they had distinctive metabolite profiles (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy and PCA analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The levels of muscle lactate were significantly greater in Mtn-/- muscle compared to that of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ consistent with a greater glycolytic phenotype.
source: Comparing the metabolic signature of the Mtn-/- muscle to the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ showed clear differences between the two groups (Figure 3C) characterised by significantly greater levels of muscle lactate in Mtn-/- muscle compared to that of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ consistent with a greater glycolytic phenotype.
evidence: The claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The levels of creatine/phosphocreatine were more pronounced in the muscle from Mtn-/- compared to Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+.
source: Furthermore the levels of creatine/phosphocreatine were also more pronounced in the muscle from Mtn-/- compared to Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+.
evidence: The claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy analysis.

claim: Errγ modification led to higher taurine and anserine content in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ animals.
source: Errγ modification led to higher taurine and anserine content in the muscle of these animals.
evidence: The claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy analysis.

claim: Errγ over-expression induced changes in levels of two key transcriptional regulators of metabolism; Perm1 and Pgc1a in Mtn-/- muscle.
source: We found that Errγ over-expression induced changes in levels of two key transcriptional regulators of metabolism; Perm1 and Pgc1a in Mtn-/- muscle (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Glut4 was lower in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to Mtn-/-.
source: We found that Glut4 and Pdk4 were lower in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to Mtn-/-.
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis.

claim: Pdk4 was lower in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to Mtn-/-.
source: We found that Glut4 and Pdk4 were lower in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to Mtn-/-.
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis.

claim: Had was higher in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/-.
source: Moreover, Had and Lpl, was higher in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/-.
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis.

claim: Lpl was higher in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/-.
source: Moreover, Had and Lpl, was higher in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/-.
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis.

claim: The expression of markers of fatty acid metabolism, Had and Lpl, were not only higher in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/- but also than in the WT condition.
source: Of particular note was the finding that the expression of markers of fatty acid metabolism, Had and Lpl, were not only higher in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/- but also than in the WT condition (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Expression of myoglobin was higher in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in WT and Mtn-/- mice.
source: We found that expression of myoglobin, which facilitates the diffusion of oxygen, and catalase, an anti-oxidant enzyme, were higher in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in WT and Mtn-/- mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Expression of catalase was higher in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in WT and Mtn-/- mice.
source: We found that expression of myoglobin, which facilitates the diffusion of oxygen, and catalase, an anti-oxidant enzyme, were higher in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in WT and Mtn-/- mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: All six genes controlling fat metabolism (Cd36, Slc25a20, Fatp1, Fabp3, Acadl, Acadm) were expressed to a higher degree in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/- and WT mice.
source: We found that all six genes were expressed to a higher degree in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/- and WT mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A number of abnormalities were found in the structure of muscle from Mtn-/- mice including heterogeneously sized sarcomeres, misaligned and disrupted Z-Lines, large inter-sarcomeric spaces and altered mitochondrial distribution and size.
source: Using transmission electron microscopy, we found a number of abnormalities in the structure of muscle from Mtn-/- mice heterogeneously sized sarcomeres, misaligned and disrupted Z-Lines, large inter-sarcomeric spaces and altered mitochondrial distribution and size (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The muscle from Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ largely lacked the ultrastructural abnormalities seen in Mtn-/- muscle.
source: In contrast, the muscle from Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ largely lacked these abnormalities (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The density of mitochondria in both sub-membrane and intrafusal locations was decreased significantly following the deletion of Mtn.
source: We found that the density of mitochondria in both sub-membrane and intrafusal locations was decreased significantly following the deletion of Mtn.
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis.

claim: The expression of Errγ significantly increased the mitochondrial density at both sub-membrane and intrafusal locations compared to Mtn-/-.
source: However, the expression of Errγ significantly increased the mitochondrial density at both locations compared to Mtn-/- and at the major site, the sub-membrane region, increased it even compared to WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis.

claim: At the sub-membrane region, Errγ expression increased mitochondrial density even compared to WT.
source: However, the expression of Errγ significantly increased the mitochondrial density at both locations compared to Mtn-/- and at the major site, the sub-membrane region, increased it even compared to WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis.

claim: Mitochondrial hypertrophy was evident in both compartments in muscle from Mtn-/-.
source: Mitochondrial hypertrophy was evident in both compartments in muscle from Mtn-/- (Figure 5B–E) and was normalized by Errγ in the sub-membrane region (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 5B-E.

claim: Mitochondrial hypertrophy in Mtn-/- was normalized by Errγ in the sub-membrane region.
source: Mitochondrial hypertrophy was evident in both compartments in muscle from Mtn-/- (Figure 5B–E) and was normalized by Errγ in the sub-membrane region (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Deletion of Mtn resulted in fewer satellite cells compared to WT.
source: We found, that deletion of Mtn resulted in fewer satellite cells compared to WT and that the number of satellite cells was even lower in the muscles of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice (Figure 6A,C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell quantification shown in Figure 6A, C and D.

claim: The number of satellite cells was even lower in the muscles of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice compared to Mtn-/-.
source: We found, that deletion of Mtn resulted in fewer satellite cells compared to WT and that the number of satellite cells was even lower in the muscles of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice (Figure 6A,C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell quantification shown in Figure 6A, C and D.

claim: Following 48 hr of culture, the number of progeny had increased in all the genotypes but the proportional relationship found in uncultured fibres persisted.
source: We found that following 48 hr of culture, the number of progeny had increased in all the genotypes but the proportional relationship found in uncultured fibres persisted (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell culture experiments shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: The number of clusters were similar in fibres from WT and Mtn-/-.
source: We found that the number of clusters were similar in fibres from WT and Mtn-/- (Figure 6G), but there were fewer clusters in the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+-derived cultures.
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell culture experiments shown in Figure 6G.

claim: There were fewer clusters in the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+-derived cultures compared to WT and Mtn-/-.
source: We found that the number of clusters were similar in fibres from WT and Mtn-/- (Figure 6G), but there were fewer clusters in the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+-derived cultures.
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell culture experiments shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The number of cells per cluster was highest in WT and lowest in the Mtn-/- with that of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ in between the two.
source: The number of cells per cluster was highest in WT and lowest in the Mtn-/- with that of the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ in between the two (Figure 6H).
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell culture experiments shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Deletion of Mtn and the introduction of Errγ did not impact on the process of differentiation.
source: Finally, we found deletion of Mtn and the introduction of Errγ did not impact on the process of differentiation (Figure 6I).
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell differentiation analysis shown in Figure 6I.

claim: There were significantly more myonuclei in the fibres of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT.
source: First, there were significantly more myonuclei in the fibres of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to WT (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by myonuclear quantification shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: The WT fibres displayed an improvement from a random distribution of 20% in myonuclear organization.
source: The WT fibres displayed an improvement from a random distribution of 20%.
evidence: The claim is supported by myonuclear organization analysis.

claim: Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ fibres had distributions that were more random, with significantly lower improvements of 10% and 4%, respectively.
source: However Mtn-/- and Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ fibres had distributions that were more random, with significantly lower improvements of 10% and 4%, respectively (Figure 6L).
evidence: The claim is supported by myonuclear organization analysis shown in Figure 6L.

claim: At D3 the muscle clearance of dying fibres was slowest in Mtn-/- compared to the other two genotypes.
source: At D3 the muscle clearance of dying fibres was slowest in Mtn-/- compared to the other two genotypes (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by regeneration experiments shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: The density of macrophages was highest in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or WT at D3.
source: We found that the density of macrophages was highest in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or WT (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by macrophage quantification shown in Figure 7C-D.

claim: The TA from Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ at the early stages of generation contained the highest number of committed muscle cells.
source: Furthermore, we found that the TA from Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ at the early stages of generation contained the highest number of committed muscle cells (Figure 7E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by myogenic progenitor quantification shown in Figure 7E-F.

claim: By D6, there was a greater degree of regeneration (size of newly formed eMHC+ fibres) in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or WT.
source: By D6, there was a greater degree of regeneration (size of newly formed eMHC+ fibres) in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or WT (Figure 7G–H) and a more advanced removal of dying fibres in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/- (Figure 7I–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by regeneration experiments shown in Figure 7G-H.

claim: There was a more advanced removal of dying fibres in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/- at D6.
source: By D6, there was a greater degree of regeneration (size of newly formed eMHC+ fibres) in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or WT (Figure 7G–H) and a more advanced removal of dying fibres in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than in Mtn-/- (Figure 7I–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by regeneration experiments shown in Figure 7I-J.

claim: There was evidence for a lower amount of cell death in the regenerating areas of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than Mtn-/- or WT mice at D6.
source: We also found evidence for a lower amount of cell death in the regenerating areas of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ than Mtn-/- or WT mice (Figure 7K–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by apoptosis analysis shown in Figure 7K-L.

claim: At D6 macrophage activity was still high in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or wild type.
source: At D6 macrophage activity was still high in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or wild type (Figure 7M–N) as were the number of committed (Myo+/Pax7-) muscle progenitor cells (Figure 7O–P).
evidence: The claim is supported by macrophage quantification shown in Figure 7M-N.

claim: At D6 the number of committed (Myo+/Pax7-) muscle progenitor cells was high in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or wild type.
source: At D6 macrophage activity was still high in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or wild type (Figure 7M–N) as were the number of committed (Myo+/Pax7-) muscle progenitor cells (Figure 7O–P).
evidence: The claim is supported by myogenic progenitor quantification shown in Figure 7O-P.

claim: There was further evidence for accelerated regeneration in the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or WT gauged by a decrease in the density of fibres still expressing eMHC at D14.
source: We found further evidence for accelerated regeneration in the Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ compared to either Mtn-/- or WT gauged by a decrease in the density of fibres still expressing eMHC (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by regeneration experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was no deficit in the size of newly regenerated fibre in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice at D14.
source: Importantly, there was no deficit in the size of newly regenerated fibre in the muscle of Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by regeneration experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: sActRIIB caused an increase in the body mass of both WT and ErrγTg/+ mice.
source: Following 8 weeks of weekly injections we found that sActRIIB caused an increase in the body mass of both WT and ErrγTg/+ mice (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 8A.

claim: sActRIIB caused an increase in muscle mass of approximately 70% in the EDL of WT and 44% in ErrγTg/+ above age-matched control animals.
source: Examination of isolated muscles showed an increase in muscle mass of approximately 70% in the EDL of WT and 44% in ErrγTg/+ above age-matched control animals (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The increase in muscle mass following sActRIIB was not due to an increase in fibre number but due to hypertrophy of all MHC fibre types.
source: The increase in muscle mass was not due to an increase in fibre number (data not shown) but due to hypertrophy of all MHC fibre types (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There was no change in the MHC fibre type composition following the injection of sActRIIB in either genotype.
source: There was no change in the MHC fibre type composition following the injection of sActRIIB in either genotype (Figure 8C and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 8C and F.

claim: Injection of sActRIIB induced a decrease in the oxidative capacity of the muscle in WT mice as indicated by a decreased proportion of SDH+ fibres.
source: However, we found that injection of sActRIIB induced a decrease in the oxidative capacity of the muscle in WT mice as indicated by a decreased proportion of SDH+ fibres (Figure 8D and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by SDH histochemistry shown in Figure 8D and G.

claim: sActRIIB did not cause a reduction in the proportion of SDH+ fibres in ErrγTg/+.
source: Strikingly, sActRIIB did not cause a reduction in the proportion of SDH+ fibres in ErrγTg/+ (Figure 8D and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by SDH histochemistry shown in Figure 8D and G.

claim: The increased oxidative capacity of the muscle was accompanied with a rise in the number of capillaries serving each fibre in the muscle from ErrγTg/+ but not WT mice following sActRIIB treatment.
source: The increased oxidative capacity of the muscle was accompanied with a rise in the number of capillaries serving each fibre in the muscle from ErrγTg/+ but not WT mice (Figure 8E and H and Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by capillary density measurements shown in Figure 8E and H and Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A central tenet of skeletal muscle biology is the existence of an inverse relationship between the oxidative fibre capacity and its size.
source: A central tenet of skeletal muscle biology is the existence of an inverse relationship between the oxidative fibre capacity and its size.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge in skeletal muscle biology.

claim: Superimposition of Estrogen-related receptor gamma (Errγ) on the myostatin (Mtn) mouse null background (Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+) results in hypertrophic muscle with a high oxidative capacity thus violating the inverse relationship between fibre size and oxidative capacity.
source: We show that superimposition of Estrogen-related receptor gamma (Errγ) on the myostatin (Mtn) mouse null background (Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+) results in hypertrophic muscle with a high oxidative capacity thus violating the inverse relationship between fibre size and oxidative capacity.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data presented in the manuscript including muscle mass, SDH staining, and metabolic profiling.

claim: Hypertrophic fibres from Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mouse showed satellite cell deficit.
source: Surprisingly, hypertrophic fibres from Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mouse showed satellite cell deficit which unexpectedly did not affect muscle regeneration.
evidence: The claim is supported by satellite cell quantification data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The satellite cell deficit in Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mouse unexpectedly did not affect muscle regeneration.
source: Surprisingly, hypertrophic fibres from Mtn-/-/ErrγTg/+ mouse showed satellite cell deficit which unexpectedly did not affect muscle regeneration.
evidence: The claim is supported by regeneration experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: Slow fibres generally have a smaller cross sectional area (CSA), contain more mitochondria which sustain a high oxidative capacity, and a denser microvascular network than fast fibres.
